USMLE-style practice · Pathology

A different epithelial response to reflux

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient with years of gastroesophageal reflux undergoes endoscopy. Distal esophageal biopsies show intestinal-type columnar epithelium containing goblet cells where stratified squamous epithelium is normally present; there is no invasion. Which adaptive change does this represent?

  1. Hypertrophy
  2. Atrophy
  3. Anaplasia
  4. Liquefactive necrosis
  5. Metaplasia
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Metaplasia

Replacement of one mature epithelial type by another is metaplasia; in this setting it is Barrett esophagus.

Understanding the options

Metaplasia
Replacement of one mature epithelial type by another is metaplasia; in this setting it is Barrett esophagus.
Hypertrophy
Hypertrophy changes size, not cell identity.
Atrophy
Atrophy reduces tissue mass and does not create goblet-cell-containing epithelium.
Anaplasia
Anaplasia denotes loss of differentiation in malignancy.
Liquefactive necrosis
Necrosis causes tissue death rather than a viable epithelial replacement.
